### What does this PR do?

Adds explicit PPO mini-batch modes to the V1 trainer and balances preserved optimizer mini-batches across data-parallel ranks.

- `fixed_rows` is the default and preserves the current verl behavior: each model targets `ppo_mini_batch_size * rollout.n` trajectory rows per optimizer update, and one UID may cross a mini-batch boundary.
- `fixed_count` is opt-in and follows the fixed-count scheduling proposed in #8099: `ppo_mini_batch_size` is a source-prompt/UID count, all trajectories from one UID stay together, and variable-output rollouts can produce variable row counts without changing the intended UID count per update.

Both modes support different actor and critic mini-batch sizes through shared GCD-sized balancing units. The legacy V0 trainer is unchanged; mini-batch construction and per-mini-batch DP balancing in this PR apply only to V1.

### Checklist Before Starting

- [x] Searched for similar PRs: [`8099 in:body`](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+8099+in%3Abody), [`mini-batch balance`](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+mini-batch+balance), and [`multi-output mini-batch`](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+multi-output+mini-batch).
- [x] Formatted the title according to the contribution guide.

This does not duplicate #6025: that PR adds grouped mini-batching to the older synchronous trainer path, while this PR adds selectable V1 modes, V1 per-mini-batch padding and DP balancing, and a variable-row worker contract.

### Test

```bash
PROTOCOL_BUFFERS_PYTHON_IMPLEMENTATION=python uv run --no-project python -m pytest tests/trainer/ppo/v1/test_minibatching_on_cpu.py tests/workers/test_engine_workers_mini_batch_trace_on_cpu.py tests/trainer/ppo/v1/test_trainer_base_on_cpu.py tests/workers/config/test_actor_config_on_cpu.py tests/workers/config/test_critic_config_on_cpu.py -q
```

Result: `34 passed, 10 skipped`.

```bash
pre-commit run --show-diff-on-failure --color=always
```

Result: all hooks passed, including Ruff, Ruff format, mypy, generated-config validation, docstring coverage, license checks, test-structure validation, naming checks, and Python compilation.

For the `fixed_rows` per-mini-batch balancing path, Qwen3-30B-A3B experiments on 4 nodes × 8 GPUs showed consistent speedups over upstream whole-batch balancing:

| Configuration | Upstream step 60 / 100 (s) | This PR step 60 / 100 (s) | Speedup |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| CP8, 128K | 224.9 / 237.9 | 191.9 / 204.7 | 1.17× |
| CP4, 64K | 331.3 / 352.9 | 291.9 / 296.3 | 1.14–1.19× |
| PP2 CP4, 128K | 254.2 / 263.6 | 224.6 / 234.3 | 1.13× |
| CP4, 128K | 414.1 / 434.9 | 352.1 / 373.1 | 1.17× |

### API and Usage Example

```yaml
trainer:
  use_v1: true
  v1:
    # fixed_rows (default) | fixed_count
    mini_batch_mode: fixed_rows
    sampler:
      # false: train only materialized UIDs
      # true: refill zero-trajectory sync groups
      sync_refill_failed_groups: false
```

`fixed_rows` pads the shared train batch to the least common multiple of the DP size and active actor/critic row mini-batch sizes. Each model then performs `padded_rows / its_row_mini_batch_size` optimizer updates per PPO epoch. With `shuffle=true` and `ppo_epochs>1`, V1 falls back to whole-train-batch DP balancing and lets workers reshuffle trajectory rows each epoch, matching current main behavior.

`fixed_count` groups by source UID, pads and balances each shared unit independently, and permits a partial final UID mini-batch when sync failures leave fewer materialized groups. If `R` UIDs produce at least one trajectory, a model performs `ceil(R / ppo_mini_batch_size)` optimizer updates per epoch. `shuffle=true` is supported for one epoch; combining it with `ppo_epochs>1` is rejected because row reshuffling would split UID groups.

### Design & Code Changes

- Add `trainer.v1.mini_batch_mode` with backward-compatible `fixed_rows` as the default and `fixed_count` as an explicit opt-in.
- Keep one V1 controller balancing pipeline: fixed-row mode forms trajectory-row units, while fixed-count mode forms UID units; both use the GCD of active actor and critic mini-batch sizes so their configured sizes may differ.
- Pad fixed-row batches once to shared actor/critic/DP divisibility. Pad each fixed-count unit independently to DP and active static micro-batch divisibility.
- Balance every preserved unit independently across actor DP ranks, then apply static-micro-batch-friendly workload ordering only within each rank's share of that unit.
- Carry controller-owned variable mini-batch layouts through TransferQueue metadata refreshes. Workers consume padded row boundaries while sequence-level loss normalization excludes synthetic rows.
- Preserve padding-aware normalization in the fixed-row multi-epoch shuffle fallback by carrying an explicit padding mask through worker shuffling and aggregating each resulting mini-batch's valid row count across DP ranks.
- Retain `trainer.v1.sampler.sync_refill_failed_groups=false` by default. Enabling it replaces zero-trajectory groups in synchronous sampling; disabling it avoids additional synchronous rollout work and lets fixed-count mode use a partial final mini-batch.
- Update generated configs and V1/PPO/GRPO documentation, and add CPU coverage for both modes, multi-output UID grouping, actor/critic size differences, partial layouts, padding, shuffle fallback, and worker normalization.
- Leave the legacy V0 `RayPPOTrainer` and its whole-batch balancing behavior unchanged.

### Checklist Before Submitting

- [x] Read the [Contribute Guide](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
- [x] Applied the required pre-commit checks.
- [x] Updated user-facing configuration and algorithm documentation.
- [x] Added CPU tests discoverable by the existing test workflows; no workflow change is required.
- [ ] Requested CI in the project Slack/Feishu channel.
- [x] Recipe submodule update is not applicable because this PR does not modify `recipe`.

### AI Assistance

Cursor's AI coding agent was used to assist with implementation, review, testing, and PR preparation. The human submitter must review every changed line and validate the design and test results before merge.

### End-to-End Qwen3.5-4B Validation

Both mini-batch modes were exercised in 64-GPU (8 nodes × 8 GPUs) Qwen3.5-4B Megatron GRPO training with TP=1, PP=1, CP=4, `rollout.n=8`, `data.train_batch_size=64`, `ppo_mini_batch_size=16`, and dynamic token batching. The validation launch configuration follows the [uni-agent Qwen3.5 dense quickstart](https://github.com/verl-project/uni-agent/blob/main/examples/quickstart/training/train_qwen3p5_dense.sh). Apart from `trainer.v1.mini_batch_mode`, the fixed-row run keeps the source configuration's `kl_loss_coef=1e-3`, while the fixed-count run uses `5e-3`; all other training settings are aligned. The agent rollout workload used the `uni_agent` framework, with SWE-rebench as the training dataset and SWE-bench Verified as the evaluation dataset. The Tracking views combine restart/resume fragments for each experiment; overlapping steps use the latest fragment.

![SWE-bench Verified reward through step 70](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/FZYsheep/0da5a8068ebb7c373d09cc0975973fc7/raw/3106a2f8896dac7f535066e03af20a42608944fe/qwen3_5_4b_64g_reward_comparison_step70.svg)

![Actor update time and mean training reward through step 70](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/FZYsheep/0da5a8068ebb7c373d09cc0975973fc7/raw/3c7e5f5c243fc1d5d1cd56440c4aa6cb46480ac1/qwen3_5_4b_64g_training_metrics_comparison_step70.svg)

**Performance-comparison note:** during the first 20 fixed-row training steps, Fused Linear Cross Entropy used verl's default Triton implementation. Starting at step 20, it used the cuBLAS-backed fused implementation, which is more efficient on A100 GPUs. Consequently, the `timing_per_token_ms/update_actor` comparison between fixed-row and fixed-count is meaningful only from step 20 onward.

The training-metric figure shows raw values as faint lines and a 5-point moving average as solid lines. These runs validate that both modes complete end-to-end training. Because the fixed-count run uses a different KL coefficient, reward differences should not be attributed solely to the mini-batch mode.

Thanks for catching this gap! I've added the ordering to V1, matching V0 while keeping it within each balancing unit to preserve PPO mini-batch boundaries.

This mainly benefits fixed-size micro-batches; dynamic batching already rebuilds and orders its micro-batches by workload. I've clarified that distinction in the PR description.

Thanks for adding the V1 ordering. There is another case worth considering when deciding where the mini-batch boundaries should be established: synthetic padding for multi-trajectory rollouts.

In V0, `RayPPOTrainer._balance_batch()` first balances the **whole batch** across DP ranks, then applies the following ordering to each rank’s **entire partition**, before workers split it into PPO mini-batches:

```python
for idx, partition in enumerate(global_partition_lst):
    partition.sort(key=lambda x: (workload_lst[x], x))
    ordered_partition = partition[::2] + partition[1::2][::-1]
    global_partition_lst[idx] = ordered_partition
```

Consequently, this ordering can change which samples belong to each subsequent mini-batch. This PR uses the same ordering pattern, but only **within each balancing unit**, preserving the mini-batch membership established beforehand.

That distinction matters for the following V1 `separate_async` case:

- `ppo_mini_batch_size=64`, `rollout.n=8`, `shuffle=False`, and no critic.
- Each local trigger samples 64 prompt groups, normally producing 512 trajectories—one global PPO mini-batch.
- If one rollout session produces an additional trajectory, the sampled batch contains **513 real trajectories**.
- `_balance_batch()` pads this to 1024 samples by appending **511 synthetic padding rows**, whose response masks are zero.

With this PR’s current `shuffle=False` path, the two global mini-batches are established before the within-unit ordering:

| Layout | Mini-batch 1: real / padding | Mini-batch 2: real / padding |
|---|---:|---:|
| Current PR | 512 / 0 | 1 / 511 |
| V0-style whole-partition ordering, DP=1 | 256 / 256 | 257 / 255 |

The second row was verified by replaying the trajectory lengths from two affected batches. It is an observed result for these inputs, rather than a general guarantee of the length-ordering heuristic.

The current PR’s ordering cannot redistribute real samples between these two updates. With DP=2, the second mini-batch still contains only one real trajectory globally: one rank receives that trajectory plus padding, while the other receives only padding. Dynamic micro-batching cannot change this composition either, since it operates inside each mini-batch.

Consequently, when training reaches the second PPO mini-batch, its optimizer update receives a loss/gradient contribution from only **one real trajectory globally**; all 511 synthetic padding rows have zero response masks and contribute no loss. With DP=2, that single effective training sample is on only one DP rank, while the other rank has no effective training samples for that update.

Thank you for further pointing out my oversight! I completely missed the scenario where prompts yield different numbers of training trajectories. From my understanding, this situation arises under two conditions:
1. When using per-prompt__rollout_n__, where each prompt generates a different number of rollouts (this appears to be rarely used at present, and VeRL training side barely supports this case).
2. Multi-trajectory rollouts(mentioned above), in which a single rollout produces multiple training trajectories.
Both scenarios may require padding. I think this is a design-induced issue. The PPO algorithm is supposed to perform one actor update per mini-batch(only consider ppo_epochs=1), yet the fixed-row partitioning approach introduces excessive padding (in the example, the number of padded trajectories is nearly equal to that of real trajectories), and causes multiple actor updates to occur within a single mini-batch.
Given the above considerations, a better approach is to adopt mini-batch partitioning by fixed count as described in https://github.com/verl-project/verl/issues/8099. This addresses both issues:
- The required number of padded trajectories is drastically reduced, changing from the original LCM(dp_size, ppo_mini_batch_size × rollout_n) to dp_size.
- Strictly enforce one actor update per mini-batch.

detail.body:
### What does this PR do?

Adds explicit PPO mini-batch modes to the V1 trainer and balances preserved optimizer mini-batches across data-parallel ranks.

- `fixed_rows` is the default and preserves the current verl behavior: each model targets `ppo_mini_batch_size * rollout.n` trajectory rows per optimizer update, and one UID may cross a mini-batch boundary.
- `fixed_count` is opt-in and follows the fixed-count scheduling proposed in #8099: `ppo_mini_batch_size` is a source-prompt/UID count, all trajectories from one UID stay together, and variable-output rollouts can produce variable row counts without changing the intended UID count per update.

Both modes support different actor and critic mini-batch sizes through shared GCD-sized balancing units. The legacy V0 trainer is unchanged; mini-batch construction and per-mini-batch DP balancing in this PR apply only to V1.

### Checklist Before Starting

- [x] Searched for similar PRs: [`8099 in:body`](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+8099+in%3Abody), [`mini-batch balance`](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+mini-batch+balance), and [`multi-output mini-batch`](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+multi-output+mini-batch).
- [x] Formatted the title according to the contribution guide.

This does not duplicate #6025: that PR adds grouped mini-batching to the older synchronous trainer path, while this PR adds selectable V1 modes, V1 per-mini-batch padding and DP balancing, and a variable-row worker contract.

### Test

```bash
PROTOCOL_BUFFERS_PYTHON_IMPLEMENTATION=python uv run --no-project python -m pytest tests/trainer/ppo/v1/test_minibatching_on_cpu.py tests/workers/test_engine_workers_mini_batch_trace_on_cpu.py tests/trainer/ppo/v1/test_trainer_base_on_cpu.py tests/workers/config/test_actor_config_on_cpu.py tests/workers/config/test_critic_config_on_cpu.py -q
```

Result: `34 passed, 10 skipped`.

```bash
pre-commit run --show-diff-on-failure --color=always
```

Result: all hooks passed, including Ruff, Ruff format, mypy, generated-config validation, docstring coverage, license checks, test-structure validation, naming checks, and Python compilation.

For the `fixed_rows` per-mini-batch balancing path, Qwen3-30B-A3B experiments on 4 nodes × 8 GPUs showed consistent speedups over upstream whole-batch balancing:

| Configuration | Upstream step 60 / 100 (s) | This PR step 60 / 100 (s) | Speedup |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| CP8, 128K | 224.9 / 237.9 | 191.9 / 204.7 | 1.17× |
| CP4, 64K | 331.3 / 352.9 | 291.9 / 296.3 | 1.14–1.19× |
| PP2 CP4, 128K | 254.2 / 263.6 | 224.6 / 234.3 | 1.13× |
| CP4, 128K | 414.1 / 434.9 | 352.1 / 373.1 | 1.17× |

### API and Usage Example

```yaml
trainer:
  use_v1: true
  v1:
    # fixed_rows (default) | fixed_count
    mini_batch_mode: fixed_rows
    sampler:
      # false: train only materialized UIDs
      # true: refill zero-trajectory sync groups
      sync_refill_failed_groups: false
```

`fixed_rows` pads the shared train batch to the least common multiple of the DP size and active actor/critic row mini-batch sizes. Each model then performs `padded_rows / its_row_mini_batch_size` optimizer updates per PPO epoch. With `shuffle=true` and `ppo_epochs>1`, V1 falls back to whole-train-batch DP balancing and lets workers reshuffle trajectory rows each epoch, matching current main behavior.

`fixed_count` groups by source UID, pads and balances each shared unit independently, and permits a partial final UID mini-batch when sync failures leave fewer materialized groups. If `R` UIDs produce at least one trajectory, a model performs `ceil(R / ppo_mini_batch_size)` optimizer updates per epoch. `shuffle=true` is supported for one epoch; combining it with `ppo_epochs>1` is rejected because row reshuffling would split UID groups.

### Design & Code Changes

- Add `trainer.v1.mini_batch_mode` with backward-compatible `fixed_rows` as the default and `fixed_count` as an explicit opt-in.
- Keep one V1 controller balancing pipeline: fixed-row mode forms trajectory-row units, while fixed-count mode forms UID units; both use the GCD of active actor and critic mini-batch sizes so their configured sizes may differ.
- Pad fixed-row batches once to shared actor/critic/DP divisibility. Pad each fixed-count unit independently to DP and active static micro-batch divisibility.
- Balance every preserved unit independently across actor DP ranks, then apply static-micro-batch-friendly workload ordering only within each rank's share of that unit.
- Carry controller-owned variable mini-batch layouts through TransferQueue metadata refreshes. Workers consume padded row boundaries while sequence-level loss normalization excludes synthetic rows.
- Preserve padding-aware normalization in the fixed-row multi-epoch shuffle fallback by carrying an explicit padding mask through worker shuffling and aggregating each resulting mini-batch's valid row count across DP ranks.
- Retain `trainer.v1.sampler.sync_refill_failed_groups=false` by default. Enabling it replaces zero-trajectory groups in synchronous sampling; disabling it avoids additional synchronous rollout work and lets fixed-count mode use a partial final mini-batch.
- Update generated configs and V1/PPO/GRPO documentation, and add CPU coverage for both modes, multi-output UID grouping, actor/critic size differences, partial layouts, padding, shuffle fallback, and worker normalization.
- Leave the legacy V0 `RayPPOTrainer` and its whole-batch balancing behavior unchanged.

### Checklist Before Submitting

- [x] Read the [Contribute Guide](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
- [x] Applied the required pre-commit checks.
- [x] Updated user-facing configuration and algorithm documentation.
- [x] Added CPU tests discoverable by the existing test workflows; no workflow change is required.
- [ ] Requested CI in the project Slack/Feishu channel.
- [x] Recipe submodule update is not applicable because this PR does not modify `recipe`.

### AI Assistance

Cursor's AI coding agent was used to assist with implementation, review, testing, and PR preparation. The human submitter must review every changed line and validate the design and test results before merge.

### End-to-End Qwen3.5-4B Validation

Both mini-batch modes were exercised in 64-GPU (8 nodes × 8 GPUs) Qwen3.5-4B Megatron GRPO training with TP=1, PP=1, CP=4, `rollout.n=8`, `data.train_batch_size=64`, `ppo_mini_batch_size=16`, and dynamic token batching. The validation launch configuration follows the [uni-agent Qwen3.5 dense quickstart](https://github.com/verl-project/uni-agent/blob/main/examples/quickstart/training/train_qwen3p5_dense.sh). Apart from `trainer.v1.mini_batch_mode`, the fixed-row run keeps the source configuration's `kl_loss_coef=1e-3`, while the fixed-count run uses `5e-3`; all other training settings are aligned. The agent rollout workload used the `uni_agent` framework, with SWE-rebench as the training dataset and SWE-bench Verified as the evaluation dataset. The Tracking views combine restart/resume fragments for each experiment; overlapping steps use the latest fragment.

![SWE-bench Verified reward through step 70](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/FZYsheep/0da5a8068ebb7c373d09cc0975973fc7/raw/3106a2f8896dac7f535066e03af20a42608944fe/qwen3_5_4b_64g_reward_comparison_step70.svg)

![Actor update time and mean training reward through step 70](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/FZYsheep/0da5a8068ebb7c373d09cc0975973fc7/raw/3c7e5f5c243fc1d5d1cd56440c4aa6cb46480ac1/qwen3_5_4b_64g_training_metrics_comparison_step70.svg)

**Performance-comparison note:** during the first 20 fixed-row training steps, Fused Linear Cross Entropy used verl's default Triton implementation. Starting at step 20, it used the cuBLAS-backed fused implementation, which is more efficient on A100 GPUs. Consequently, the `timing_per_token_ms/update_actor` comparison between fixed-row and fixed-count is meaningful only from step 20 onward.

The training-metric figure shows raw values as faint lines and a 5-point moving average as solid lines. These runs validate that both modes complete end-to-end training. Because the fixed-count run uses a different KL coefficient, reward differences should not be attributed solely to the mini-batch mode.

Thanks for adding the V1 ordering. There is another case worth considering when deciding where the mini-batch boundaries should be established: synthetic padding for multi-trajectory rollouts.

In V0, `RayPPOTrainer._balance_batch()` first balances the **whole batch** across DP ranks, then applies the following ordering to each rank’s **entire partition**, before workers split it into PPO mini-batches:

```python
for idx, partition in enumerate(global_partition_lst):
    partition.sort(key=lambda x: (workload_lst[x], x))
    ordered_partition = partition[::2] + partition[1::2][::-1]
    global_partition_lst[idx] = ordered_partition
```

Consequently, this ordering can change which samples belong to each subsequent mini-batch. This PR uses the same ordering pattern, but only **within each balancing unit**, preserving the mini-batch membership established beforehand.

That distinction matters for the following V1 `separate_async` case:

- `ppo_mini_batch_size=64`, `rollout.n=8`, `shuffle=False`, and no critic.
- Each local trigger samples 64 prompt groups, normally producing 512 trajectories—one global PPO mini-batch.
- If one rollout session produces an additional trajectory, the sampled batch contains **513 real trajectories**.
- `_balance_batch()` pads this to 1024 samples by appending **511 synthetic padding rows**, whose response masks are zero.

With this PR’s current `shuffle=False` path, the two global mini-batches are established before the within-unit ordering:

| Layout | Mini-batch 1: real / padding | Mini-batch 2: real / padding |
|---|---:|---:|
| Current PR | 512 / 0 | 1 / 511 |
| V0-style whole-partition ordering, DP=1 | 256 / 256 | 257 / 255 |

The second row was verified by replaying the trajectory lengths from two affected batches. It is an observed result for these inputs, rather than a general guarantee of the length-ordering heuristic.

The current PR’s ordering cannot redistribute real samples between these two updates. With DP=2, the second mini-batch still contains only one real trajectory globally: one rank receives that trajectory plus padding, while the other receives only padding. Dynamic micro-batching cannot change this composition either, since it operates inside each mini-batch.

Consequently, when training reaches the second PPO mini-batch, its optimizer update receives a loss/gradient contribution from only **one real trajectory globally**; all 511 synthetic padding rows have zero response masks and contribute no loss. With DP=2, that single effective training sample is on only one DP rank, while the other rank has no effective training samples for that update.
